findings.body:
**Refuse `RandomizedDelaySec` in timer templates, or add it to the completion bound.**

`_timer_bound_seconds` reads only `OnCalendar`, `OnUnitActiveSec`, `OnUnitInactiveSec`, and `AccuracySec`, so a `RandomizedDelaySec` value is ignored. systemd can add that delay to each timer elapse. `declared_inventory` does not reject it: `validate_unit_template` checks only the `@CRQ_ROOT@` placeholder. A template that declares the key therefore produces a `timer_bound_seconds` that is too small. `_completion_budget` uses that value for `required = service_timeout + bound + COMPLETION_MARGIN_SECONDS`, and that value becomes the completion window. A healthy second completion that arrives after the window can then be treated as a failed switch.

No current template declares the key, so this affects only a future template change. The default `AccuracySec` of 1 min is covered by the existing 60 s margin, so it is not a separate defect.

The simplest fix is to refuse the key where timer templates are read:

<details>
<summary>🛡️ Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
             timer_bound = _timer_bound_seconds(timer_text)
+            if _section_values(timer_text, "Timer", "RandomizedDelaySec"):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    "timer template declares RandomizedDelaySec: " + timer)
```

</details>
findings.title: Refuse `RandomizedDelaySec` in timer templates, or add it to the completion bound.

findings.body:
**Undeclared CRQ references make every switch refuse.**

`_scan_dependencies` walks the whole unit directory (unit-live-binding.py:388-423). At line 449, any CRQ name in a dependency directive is flagged when its source is undeclared, even if the name is in `expected`. A directive in another unit's file therefore reaches `foreign`. For example, while switching `crq-tick.service`, `crq-publisher.timer:7` (`Unit=crq-publisher.service`) is flagged because that file is not declared and `crq-publisher.service` is not in the switched set. `crq-publisher.path:6` (`Wants=crq-publisher.service`), `crq-repair.timer:4`, and `crq-backfill.timer:6` have the same effect. `_discover` refuses when `foreign` is non-empty (unit-adapter.py:712-715). With those units installed in the user unit directory, every switch can refuse this way.

A declared template that names a unit in `expected` is already not flagged at line 449. The defect is that undeclared files naming other CRQ units are treated as foreign activators of the switched unit.

Restrict the undeclared-source flag to names in `expected`. Keep the flag for declared sources that name units outside `expected`. Before changing the condition, confirm that the drop-in handling at line 533 is covered.
findings.title: Undeclared CRQ references make every switch refuse.

findings.body:
**Send the helper's success narration to stderr.**

`apps/crq-python/ops/prepare-host.py:821` writes `completed <operation>; no units started` to stdout on every successful run. Doctrine I1 requires stdout to carry one machine-readable JSON artifact and narration to go to stderr. Any caller that parses stdout receives prose instead of JSON. The helper also has no `--json` option, so `--json` fails argument parsing.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-    print('completed ' + args.operation + '; no units started')
+    print('completed ' + args.operation + '; no units started', file=sys.stderr)
```

`main()` imports `sys` only inside the `argv is None` branch. That import makes `sys` a local name for the whole function. Add a module-level `import sys` and remove the local import so that `sys.stderr` resolves on every path.

</details>
findings.title: Send the helper's success narration to stderr.
